title: Vertical Sump / Cantilever Pump
model_title: Vertical Sump / Cantilever Pump (No Submerged Bearings)

introduction.definition: A vertical sump (cantilever) pump hangs a volute pump into a sump or tank from a mounting plate, with the motor above. In the cantilever design the shaft is supported only by bearings above the mounting plate, so there are no submerged bearings to wear — ideal for dirty or corrosive liquids and dry-running sumps.
applications: Alumina refinery floor sumps and liquor tanks
key_points: Can run with the sump level falling to the casing
Setting depth limited by shaft stiffness

classification.api_610_type: VS5 (cantilever sump pump); VS4 has line-shaft bearings

introduction.summary: A vertical pump for sumps and pits where the hydraulic end hangs in the liquid but every bearing is above the mounting plate. A short, very stiff shaft carries the impeller as a cantilever, so there are no submerged bushings to wear out on abrasive or corrosive liquids, and the pump tolerates running dry when the sump empties. Liquid enters the bottom of the volute and leaves up a separate discharge pipe.

video_tutorials.title: Vertical Sump / Cantilever Pump — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Vertical Sump / Cantilever Pump.
A vertical sump (cantilever) pump hangs a volute pump into a sump or tank from a mounting plate, with the motor above.
In the cantilever design the shaft is supported only by bearings above the mounting plate, so there are no submerged bearings to wear — ideal for dirty or corrosive liquids and dry-running sumps.
Typical applications include process drains and effluent sumps; chemical and acid sumps; mineral processing spillage sumps; alumina refinery floor sumps and liquor tanks.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Volute Casing (Submerged), Semi-Open Impeller, Cantilever Shaft (Large Diameter).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Vertical Sump / Cantilever Pump works.
Liquid enters the bottom suction of the submerged volute casing.
The impeller raises pressure; the volute turns the flow into the discharge pipe.
The discharge pipe carries the liquid up through the mounting plate.
A stiff, large-diameter shaft is supported only by the bearing housing above the plate.
The support column carries the casing from the mounting plate.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Vertical Sump / Cantilever Pump.
Check bearing temperature and vibration.
Grease bearings.
Lift unit; inspect impeller and casing for wear and corrosion.
Watch for shaft deflection / rubbing: vibration. Common cause: operation far from bep.
Watch for wear and corrosion: falling performance. Common cause: abrasive or corrosive sump liquid.
Watch for vortexing: noise, air entrainment. Common cause: low level.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
